key: Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct.
s: After forbidding believers to mock, spy and backbite, the surah addresses all humankind; al-Tabari, on 49:13, reads the tribes as made for knowing near and distant kin, not as merit before God, and the noblest as the most God-fearing, not the grandest house.

evidence.words: إنما جعلنا هذه الشعوب والقبائل لكم أيها الناس، ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب القرابة منه وبعده، لا لفضيلة لكم في ذلك، وقُربة تقرّبكم إلى الله، بل أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم … إن أكرمكم أيها الناس عند ربكم، أشدّكم اتقاء له بأداء فرائضه واجتناب معاصيه، لا أعظمكم بيتا ولا أكثركم عشيرة
evidence.gloss: We made these nations and tribes for you, O people, only so that you might know one another by nearness and distance of kinship, not for any merit of yours in that, nor as a nearness bringing you close to God; rather the noblest of you with God is the most God-fearing … The noblest of you, O people, with your Lord is the one who fears Him most, by performing His duties and avoiding disobedience to Him, not the one with the greatest house or the largest clan.
evidence.licence: classical text public domain; digitisation by Tarteel (QUL), no licence stated; short excerpt with attribution

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Hujurat 49:13, at 4624), beginning after ‘O mankind!’ and stopping before the closing sentence. In his comment on 49:13 al-Tabari says in his own voice that the nations and tribes were made so people know one another in nearness and distance of kinship, not for any merit or nearness to God in that, and that the noblest with God is the most God-fearing, not the one with the greatest house or largest clan; the sentence paraphrases both without addition. Plain sense matches 49:11 to 49:12 (deriding, spying, backbiting) and the turn to ‘O mankind’. Entry-check ok, no changes.
